products.name: Hour One
products.note: AI avatar video; virtual presenters; enterprise video; likeness consent; Israeli vendor

reading.body:
Hour One is an Israeli vendor of AI avatar video, sold to enterprises for virtual presenters, with likeness consent noted as part of the product.

The company sits in video generation and editing, a category where the output is a rendered clip rather than text or code. That distinction matters for infrastructure because video generation is the most compute-hungry common AI workload per unit of output, and avatar video adds a persistent identity layer on top of it. The likeness consent note is the only governance detail in the record, and it points at the part of this product that is not purely technical: a synthetic presenter is a person's face, licensed.

What the data does not contain is anything about how Hour One runs. There is no model, no hosting arrangement, no chip, no data center, no power contract, and no cost figure. The record also carries no funding, headcount, customer count, or revenue, and no cases or MCP entry, so nothing here establishes scale or adoption. The refresh interval of 90 days means this snapshot is a point in time, not a trend.

The honest reading is narrow. This is a company profile with one product and one category, enough to place Hour One in the avatar video market and not enough to say anything about the compute or power behind it.
